title: Nextcloud sync clients poll instead of being pushed changes
body:
`blueprints/nextcloud-s3-oidc/` (`services.yml`, `x-catena.yml`, `test.yml`). The app runs no notify_push (Client Push)
service, so every desktop and mobile client polls the server for changes, which costs CPU and database load per client.
notify_push is a Nextcloud app plus a push server shipped as a binary in the app; the server listens on 7867, reads
`config.php` (or `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `NEXTCLOUD_URL`), needs Redis, and is set up with
`occ app:enable notify_push` then `occ notify_push:setup https://<host>/push`, which runs its own checks
([README](https://github.com/nextcloud/notify_push)). Its troubleshooting covers the push server needing to be a trusted
proxy (`trusted_proxies`, `HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR` in `forwarded_for_headers`). At pick-up: which image runs the binary (the
Nextcloud image with the app's binary, or a published one) and how `/push/` on the app's hostname reaches it with
WebSocket upgrade.

- **Behaviour:** a Nextcloud install runs the push service by default; sync clients receive changes without polling, and
  the app's settings page shows Client Push configured.
- **Security notes:** a new WebSocket route `/push/` on the app's public hostname; the push service holds the same
  database and Redis credentials as Nextcloud.
- **Acceptance:** `app-tests` for nextcloud-s3-oidc passes a leg where `occ notify_push:setup https://<host>/push`
  succeeds after install and after an update. The `test.yml` change goes in its own PR, merged when app-tests is green.

title: app-main judges the main commits of a calling app repository
body:
A second app repository that pushes straight to its `main` calls this repository's `app-ci` on pull requests only, so a
commit of its `main` reaches the tests and a tag with no stack file, CVE, provenance or ClamAV check; `app-tag.yml` holds
a tag back for a missing `app-ci` in this catalog alone. `.github/workflows/app-main.yml` runs app-ci per commit on this
repository's `main`.

- **Behaviour:** `app-main.yml` (or app-ci) can be called for another repository's push to `main`: each commit is judged
  from its parent, only the commits that passed go on to the tests, and a tag needs app-ci at the app's last change.
- **Security notes:** none new.
- **Acceptance:** a caller's two-commit push with one failing commit: that commit gets `app-ci` failure and no
  `app-tests` status, the other is tagged. Workflow changes need a person with the Workflows permission.

- **Behaviour:** `tested` names such an app as held by app-ci, so a caller can tell it from an app that can be tagged.

title: A downgraded app reads changed forever, and a merged pull request is tested again
body:
Two paths run an app's lifecycle on files a run already judged:

- A pull request that passed is tested again on `main` after its squash merge, on the same app files.
- After an image downgrade on `main`, `lib/versions.py tested` reports the app `changed` against the higher tag forever,
  so the nightly tests it each time its window comes round and tags `<lower>-N` again; hosts never take the lower tag
  either.

- **Behaviour:** a run whose app files (and the harness and `lib/`) match a run that already has a verdict reuses it; a
  downgrade is reported as such and leaves the nightly list.
- **Security notes:** a reused verdict must be keyed by content the run cannot choose (tree hashes), never by a name.
- **Acceptance:** `tests/test_versions.py` cases for a downgrade; a squash-merged pull request whose app files match
  posts the earlier verdict without a lifecycle job.
